short_title: Connective Tissue Proper — Cells, Matrix, Fibres & Types

segments.script: The 'glue' of your body isn't just inert packing material. Proper connective tissue is alive, active, and defending you every second.
segments.video_prompt: SEM-style cinematic zoom into loose connective tissue matrix. Collagen fibres crisscross while a mast cell releases granule clouds and a macrophage extends amoeboid pseudopodia toward bacterial debris. Dramatic amber and teal colouring, deep-field microscopy style.

segments.script: Three components: Cells — fibroblasts (synthesise fibres and matrix), mast cells (histamine and heparin), histocytes (macrophages), lymphocytes (immune surveillance), plasma cells (antibodies). Matrix — proteoglycan ground substance. Fibres — collagen (white, tensile strength), elastic (yellow, extensible), reticular (colourless, fine framework). Loose types: areolar tissue (body packing, all cell and fibre types) and adipose (white fat — single droplet, peripheral nucleus; brown fat — multiple droplets, many mitochondria for thermogenesis). Dense types: white fibrous (tendons muscle-to-bone, ligaments bone-to-bone), elastic CT, reticular CT (lymph node framework).
segments.video_prompt: Three-panel SEM render: collagen bundles (parallel white cables), elastic fibres (wavy yellow), reticular network (grey branching). Below: H&E histology comparison — areolar tissue (loose matrix with cells) vs. adipose (clear lipid vacuoles with peripheral signet-ring nuclei). Then a compact summary table appears showing all cell types and their functions as neon-labeled rows. Dark background, bright callout labels.
